questions.prompt: The component's `imports` array is `[AvatarComponent]`. What happens when the user clicks the username?

options.text: Nothing: without `RouterLink` in `imports`, `routerLink` is just an unknown HTML attribute
The build fails: `routerLink` is not a known property
It navigates: the router is provided for the whole app

questions.explanation: A plain `routerLink="..."` attribute compiles fine even when the directive is missing, so nothing warns you. Add `RouterLink` to the component's `imports`. (A binding like `[routerLink]` would fail the build instead.)

code.label: profile.component.ts

options.text: Still noa_k's profile: the router reuses the same component, and the snapshot was read only once
dan_r's profile: the component is created again for the new URL
An error: the snapshot is out of date

questions.explanation: When only a parameter changes, the router keeps the existing component. A snapshot is read once, so it never sees the new value. Use a value that updates: `toSignal(this.route.paramMap...)`, or an input bound with `withComponentInputBinding()`.

`'noa_k'`: inputs with the same name as a parameter are filled automatically
An error: routed components can't have inputs

questions.explanation: Binding route params to inputs is opt-in: `provideRouter(routes, withComponentInputBinding())`.

questions.prompt: The page throws an error as soon as the comment form appears. Click the buggy line.

context.label: comment-form.component.ts

code.label: comment-form.component.html
code.source:
<form class="comment-form" [formGroup]="commentForm" (ngSubmit)="submit()">
  <input class="comment-input" formControlName="text" placeholder="Add a comment…">
  <button class="post-button" type="submit" [disabled]="commentForm.invalid">Post</button>
</form>

questions.explanation: `formControlName` must match a key in the group. The control is called `commentText`, so Angular can't find a control named `text`.

questions.prompt: The component's `imports` array is empty. What happens when you build?

options.text: It fails: `formGroup` isn't a known property of `form`
It builds, but submitting reloads the page
It builds: forms work in every component

questions.explanation: The reactive forms directives come from `ReactiveFormsModule`. Add it to the component's `imports`.

questions.prompt: Clicking "Cancel" posts the comment. Click the line that causes it.

code.label: comment-form.component.html
code.source:
<form class="comment-form" [formGroup]="commentForm" (ngSubmit)="submit()">
  <input class="comment-input" formControlName="commentText">
  <button class="cancel-button" (click)="cancel()">Cancel</button>
  <button class="post-button" type="submit">Post</button>
</form>

questions.explanation: A button inside a form without a `type` is a submit button, so clicking it also submits the form. Give it `type="button"`.

questions.prompt: Match each piece of router setup with what it does.

pairs.right: Route parameters such as `:username` arrive in the page as inputs
Blocks the route until the guard allows it, for example when logged out
Loads the page's code only when the user first opens it
Sends any unknown URL back to the feed

questions.explanation: These four cover most of what the Instagram app needs from the router. Routes are matched from top to bottom, so the `**` route always goes last.
